title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & cost breakdown
next_steps: Sofia to send pricing sheet and SKU-level cost breakdown by 2025-12-10
Liam to share short demo video showing per-route dashboards and how to set alerts
EdgePoint to provide sample traffic patterns / route list for a pilot
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting w/ SE + EdgePoint infra — target week of 2025-12-15
action_items: Sofia Chen — send pricing and examples of Dedicated vs Hosted cost models — due 2025-12-10
Liam Patel — share console video clip + sample dashboard JSON — due 2025-12-09
Carlos Mendes — share list of top 10 API routes + expected qps and SLAs — due 2025-12-12
summary: AE and SE from Redwood walked EdgePoint through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown features. Main asks: detailed pricing by route, pilot with traffic patterns, and security docs. Customer cares about per-route latency SLOs, cost allocation across teams, and private deployment options.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 50 minutes. i'm sofia from redwood and liam will run through the console walkthrough. um quick intros?
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: carlos here, head of ml at edgepoint. Priya and avery from infra are on. Sam from procurement might drop in for pricing q's.
[00:17] Sofia Chen: great, goal is to show our usage analytics, the per-route dashboards, and how cost breakdown maps to routes and teams. we'll keep it practical.
[00:30] Liam Patel: i'll share screen in a sec. top-level — console shows token-level cost, latency p50/p95, throughput per route, and a cost attribution layer so you can slice by team or product.
[00:45] Priya Rao: ah nice, is that automatic or do we need to tag routes?
[00:50] Liam Patel: it's a mix — we auto-detect routes from your API keys and paths, but we also let you add metadata tags (team, product, env) either via headers or in the routing config. that makes chargeback simple.
[01:05] Carlos Mendes: can you show how it looks for a high-qps route, like our chat-summarize endpoint? that's where most token spend is.
[01:12] Liam Patel: sure. opening per-route dashboard now — you see the route selector on the left, then a timeline of requests, tokens, cost estimate, and latency buckets. the cost estimate is driven by model used + token counts and any quantization/accelerator multiplier.
[01:30] [screen noise / brief pause]
[01:37] Liam Patel: here we have the token breakdown — input tokens vs generated tokens, per-hour cost, and a projected monthly run-rate based on last 30 days. note the prediction assumes your current batching and kv-cache hit rate.
[01:55] Priya Rao: kv cache hit rate — is that computed automatically? we do some client-side caching today.
[02:00] Liam Patel: yes, we compute automatic KV cache hit rate on the serving side and surface both prefix cache and per-request hits. if you have client caching you'll see lower origin tokens. we also show hypothetical savings if you enable prefix caching or increase batch window.
[02:18] Carlos Mendes: show me a cost scenario comparing hosted vs dedicated? we need predictable spend.
[02:24] Liam Patel: switching to the cost models panel — hosted shows variable per-token pricing; dedicated shows reserved vGPU pools, a fixed monthly commit and lower per-token execution cost. we show a crossover point: for your estimated qps, dedicated becomes cheaper after X tokens/day. (note: numbers are illustrative.)
[02:45] Sam (Procurement): is there a way to export the per-route cost for our finance team? csv or spreasheet?
[02:50] Sofia Chen: yes exports — csv/ parquet and direct integrations to billing systems are available for enterprise plans. we'll include a sample export in the follow-up.
[03:05] Priya Rao: what about burst capacity? we sometimes have spikes during batch jobs.
[03:10] Liam Patel: dedicated supports burst capacity configs — you can configure autoscale policies. the console shows capacity usage and recommended autoscale settings based on historical peaks.
[03:25] Carlos Mendes: how precise is the per-token cost? we use quantized models so execution cost varies by model flavor.
[03:32] Liam Patel: we tag each serving variant (quantized/float16/ggml-like) with a model cost multiplier. the cost calc includes that multiplier and GPU time estimate. there can be variance +/- a few percent depending on kernel mix.
[03:50] [brief crosstalk]
[03:55] Priya Rao: show the alerts piece. i want to be notified if a route crosses a cost threshold.
[04:00] Liam Patel: over to alerts — you can set alerts on tokens/hour, cost/day, or latency p95. alerts can be wired to slack/email/webhooks and you can set runbooks to automatically throttle or route to a cheaper model.
[04:18] Carlos Mendes: automatically route to cheaper model? example please.
[04:22] Liam Patel: yes, smart routing policy. e.g., for non-llm-critical responses you can fallback to a smaller quantized model or warm-start with a cached response. we demoed this in a PoC with a customer who saved ~35% monthly spend.
[04:40] Sofia Chen: quick note — we'll send the PoC spreadsheet that shows the math for that 35% savings.
[04:46] Priya Rao: okay good. security wise we need audit logs and KMS support.
[04:50] Sofia Chen: we have SOC2, KMS/HSM integration, and per-request audit logs with SSO/SAML and RBAC. liam can share the security pack after.
[04:58] Liam Patel: yeah i'll drop the security doc. also the per-route logs include request/response IDs for tracing, and you can enable redaction for PII.
[05:12] Carlos Mendes: in the per-route view can we group by team? we want to allocate costs to product lines.
[05:18] Liam Patel: yes grouping by tags or header metadata is supported; the chargeback UI lets you aggregate monthly spend by tag.
[05:26] Priya Rao: how does this align with our cloud billing? we want to reconcile with AWS cost numbers.
[05:32] Liam Patel: exports can be mapped to your internal chargeback — we provide both token-level line items and a reconciliation guide. Dedicated customers can get detailed GPU utilization reports too.
[05:44] [06:00] Sofia Chen: demo note — we're going to show a real customer example: route "summarize-chat" and the monthly cost breakdown across dev/staging/prod.
[06:08] Liam Patel: showing sample route — you can click into an hour window and replay requests or inspect a single request's token trail. there are occasional transcription mismatches in the logs (auto transcribe), so we always recommend request IDs for debugging.
[06:28] Carlos Mendes: about pilot — what do you need from us?
[06:31] Sofia Chen: ideal pilot: you give top 10 routes, expected qps and SLA targets; we run a 2-week pilot on hosted with our monitoring and provide the cost/throughput report; if it looks promising we can scope Dedicated.
[06:45] Priya Rao: can the pilot be in our VPC? network constraints sometimes block hosted traffic.
[06:50] Liam Patel: yes we offer Private with VPC peering or on-prem package for pilots. it depends on level of data isolation you need.
[06:58] Carlos Mendes: latency — p95 requirements are 250ms for interactive routes. can you meet that?
[07:03] Liam Patel: depends on model and sequence length; with batching and KV cache warm we often hit sub-200ms p95 on optimized kernels for instruct-sized requests. we can run a benchmark with your payload to validate.
[07:18] Sam (Procurement): pricing question — what's included in the enterprise plan?
[07:22] Sofia Chen: enterprise includes higher retention for analytics, audit logs, SSO, custom SLAs, and export connectors. pricing is usage + optional committed Dedicated fees. we'll send the SKUs.
[07:36] Priya Rao: one more on cost breakdown — can we map cost to GitHub teams or JIRA projects?
[07:41] Liam Patel: yep, as long as you supply a tag mapping or include header metadata in requests, the console can map to arbitrary dimensions — projects, teams, cost center.
[07:55] [08:00] Sofia Chen: okay wrapping up, recap of next steps: sofia will send pricing and sample export, liam will share short video and security pack, carlos will share routes.
[08:12] Carlos Mendes: sounds good. appreciate the walkthrough.
[08:16] Priya Rao: thanks, we'll review and come back with a pilot request.
[08:20] Sofia Chen: perfect — we'll target the pilot kickoff week of 2025-12-15 and i'll include a proposed agenda. thanks everyone.
[08:28] [meeting ends]
